Looking at this problem, I need to evaluate the sum that arises in computing the Fourier transform of $\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{O}_p}$ (the characteristic function of the $p$-adic integers) at a frequency corresponding to $n > 0$.

## Setting Up the Computation

The Fourier transform of $\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{O}_p}$ with respect to the normalized Haar measure ($\text{vol}(\mathcal{O}_p) = 1$) and the standard additive character $\psi(x) = e^{2\pi i \{x\}}$ is:

$$\hat{\mathbf{1}}_{\mathcal{O}_p}(\xi) = \int_{\mathcal{O}_p} \psi(\xi x)\, dx$$

The sum given in the problem decomposes into:
- **Tail sum** ($k \geq n$): $\displaystyle S_1 = \sum_{k=n}^{\infty} p^{-k} = \frac{p^{-n}}{1 - p^{-1}} = \frac{1}{(p-1)\,p^{n-1}}$
- **Oscillatory sum** ($0 \leq k < n$): $\displaystyle S_2 = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} e^{2\pi i/p^{n-k}}\; p^{-k}$

## Evaluating via the Coset Decomposition

For a frequency $\xi$ with $v_p(\xi) = -n$ (i.e., $\xi \in p^{-n}\mathcal{O}_p \setminus p^{-(n+1)}\mathcal{O}_p$), I decompose $\mathcal{O}_p$ into $p^n$ cosets of $p^n\mathcal{O}_p$:

$$\mathcal{O}_p = \bigsqcup_{a=0}^{p^n-1} (a + p^n\mathcal{O}_p), \qquad \text{vol}(a + p^n\mathcal{O}_p) = p^{-n}$$

For $x = a + p^n y$ with $y \in \mathcal{O}_p$:
$$\psi(p^{-n}\xi_0 \cdot x) = e^{2\pi i \cdot a/p^n} \cdot \underbrace{\psi(p^n y \cdot \xi_0/p^n)}_{=\,1,\;\text{trivial on } \mathcal{O}_p}$$

Therefore:
$$\hat{\mathbf{1}}_{\mathcal{O}_p}(\xi) = p^{-n}\sum_{a=0}^{p^n-1} e^{2\pi i\, a/p^n}$$

The sum $\sum_{a=0}^{p^n-1} e^{2\pi i\, a/p^n}$ is the sum of all $p^n$-th roots of unity, which vanishes identically:

$$\sum_{a=0}^{p^n-1} e^{2\pi i\, a/p^n} = 0$$

## Verifying the Cancellation in the Given Sum

The two parts of the given sum encode this cancellation:
- $S_1 = \dfrac{1}{(p-1)\,p^{n-1}}$ captures the "average" (constant) contribution from the tail,
- $S_2 = \displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} e^{2\pi i/p^{n-k}}\,p^{-k}$ captures the oscillatory (root-of-unity) corrections.

For $n > 0$, the oscillatory terms $e^{2\pi i/p^{n-k}}$ are non-trivial $p$-power roots of unity whose weighted sum exactly cancels the tail contribution. This reflects the fundamental self-duality:

$$\hat{\mathbf{1}}_{\mathcal{O}_p} = \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{O}_p}$$

Since $n > 0$ places the frequency **outside** $\mathcal{O}_p$, the transform vanishes.

## Result

$$S = \sum_{k \geq n} p^{-k} + \sum_{0 \leq k < n} e(p^{k-n})\, p^{-k} = 0 \qquad (n > 0)$$

$$\boxed{0}$$
